finding_quote: A shadow host inside a hidden container gets its shadow content hidden individually.
_prompt:
You are matching code-review findings against a known bug. Reply with ONLY a JSON object.

KNOWN BUG: When the target is itself a shadow host, its own shadow content is hidden.

Rules:
- Answer "yes" only if the text describes THIS specific bug: the same faulty behaviour in the same situation. A finding about a nearby but different behaviour (another header, another edge case, a different race) is "no".
- A finding that says the behaviour was checked and PASSED, or that the code handles it correctly, is "no".
- Wording does not matter; the behaviour does.
- For handoffs: count only text that tells the implementor to fix this bug (a reported finding, a fix instruction). Restated acceptance criteria that merely describe the desired behaviour do NOT count as carrying the finding unless the handoff ties them to a reported failure.

=== REVIEW 1 FINDINGS ===
- [blocking] A shadow host inside a hidden container gets its shadow content hidden individually. Probe: body > `input` (target, light), body > `div` D, D > shadow host H > `button`. `ariaHideOutside([t])` gives D `aria-hidden="true"` but the button inside H's shadow also gets `aria-hidden="true"`. Same for a sibling host nested in a hidden sibling host's light DOM (P13). The control with a plain nested element (no host) passes, so the bug is specific to hosts. Cause: ShadowTreeWalker's `_acceptNode` returns ACCEPT for every host without consulting the filter. `nextNode` then REJECTs the host, but the parent check only tests whether the shadow root's host is hidden, and the host is not hidden, so its shadow children are accepted. Fix idea: when a host is rejected because an ancestor is hidden, reject its shadow children too (e.g., check hidden ancestry through hosts rather than only the direct host).
- [minor] The "with shadow DOM" block enables the flag in `beforeAll` and never disables it. The flag-off test passes only because it runs first in file order. A `disableShadowDOM`-style reset or a comment would make this robust.
- [minor] Design note, not reproduced as a bug: while a nested call is active, the first call's roots are not observed (only the top observer is). Content added to the first call's shadow root during nesting is not hidden. This matches the spec's "disconnects the first's observers" wording.
=== IMPLEMENTOR HANDOFF 1 (sent after review 1) ===
GOAL: Fix one reproduced bug in the uncommitted change in /tmp/ff-eval-mcau30vq/workspace (`git diff -- packages/`) that makes `ariaHideOutside` (packages/@react-aria/overlays/src/ariaHideOutside.ts) shadow-DOM aware when `shadowDOM()` is on.

Bug (reproduced): body > input (target, light DOM); body > div D; D > shadow host H; H.shadowRoot > button. With enableShadowDOM(), `ariaHideOutside([input])` hides D (correct) but also gives the button inside H's shadow root its own aria-hidden="true" (wrong: nothing inside an already-hidden container should get its own aria-hidden, same as the light-DOM rule). Same for a host that is a light child of a hidden sibling host. Cause: ShadowTreeWalker enters every host's shadow root regardless of the filter's REJECT; acceptNode's parent check for top-level shadow children only checks whether the direct host is in hiddenNodes, and here H wasn't hidden (it was rejected because its ancestor D is hidden).

FILES: packages/@react-aria/overlays/src/ariaHideOutside.ts (acceptNode, the `parent` fallback for shadow-root children); packages/@react-aria/utils/src/shadowdom/ShadowTreeWalker.ts (read only); tests in packages/@react-aria/overlays/test/ariaHideOutside.test.js ("with shadow DOM" describe at the end).

CONSTRAINTS: Only change those two overlays files. Keep the flag-off path identical to the original (gate any new logic on `shadowDOM()`). Suggested fix: for a node whose parentNode is a ShadowRoot, reject it if the host or any ancestor of the host (walking up through parentElement and across shadow roots to their hosts, stopping at `root`) is in hiddenNodes — keep the role="row" exception semantics for the direct parent. Keep it cheap (only runs for top-level shadow-root children). Don't run `yarn install`; don't touch package.json, yarn.lock, FEATURE_FLOW.md. Write the failing tests first (both cases above, plus revert restores everything), see them fail, then fix.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- With enableShadowDOM() on, for a target inside a shadow root, every element outside the targets is hidden: siblings of the target inside its shadow root, siblings inside every enclosing shadow root (nested hosts), and light DOM siblings of the outermost host. Each shadow host on the path to a target stays visible (no aria-hidden, no inert), and the target and its descendants stay visible.
- Same with `shouldUseInert: true`: hidden elements get `inert`, hosts on the path and targets do not.
- After ariaHideOutside runs, an element appended anywhere in a target's shadow root, or in any shadow root enclosing a target, or in the light DOM, gets hidden (await waitFor). An element appended inside a target stays visible. An element appended inside an already-hidden container gets no aria-hidden of its own (same as the light DOM rule).
- Live announcers (`data-live-announcer="true"`) and top-layer elements (`data-react-aria-top-layer="true"`) stay visible both when present before ariaHideOutside runs and when added afterwards inside a target's shadow root or enclosing shadow root.
- Targets in different shadow roots work: e.g. an input in shadow root A and its popover in shadow root B (sibling hosts in body): both targets and both hosts stay visible; everything else in A, in B, and in the body is hidden; content added later in A or B is hidden.
- The returned function restores every element it hid (aria-hidden / inert removed, elements that already had aria-hidden="true" before keep it) and stops observing all roots: content appended to any of those shadow roots after revert stays visible.
- Nested calls (observerStack) keep working with shadow roots: a second ariaHideOutside call disconnects the first's observers on all its roots; reverting the second re-observes the first's roots (content added then in a shadow root is hidden again by the first).
- With shadow DOM support off, nothing changes: all existing ariaHideOutside tests pass unchanged, and a test (run before the flag is enabled) shows that with the flag off, siblings inside a target's shadow root are NOT hidden (documents current behavior).
- `keepVisible` still works for an element inside a shadow root (e.g. added later as a sibling in the shadow root after keepVisible was called, it isn't hidden).
- Existing repo checks pass: `yarn jest packages/@react-aria/overlays`, `yarn eslint` on changed files, `yarn check-types`.
